content:
jamie: seeing ~12 GPUs NotReady in the us-west preemptible GPU pool since the last autoscaler scale-up. pods are stuck Pending and CA won't add more nodes because it thinks there are unready nodes. :confused:

alex: can you paste `kubectl get nodes` and the describe for one of the NotReady nodes?

jamie: here — small excerpt:
```
NAME                                STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
gke-gpu-preempt-3-abcde             NotReady   <none>   12m   v1.26.3
```
and `kubectl describe node gke-gpu-preempt-3-abcde` shows the kubelet condition: KernelDeadlock? Not exactly but Device plugin failing: No devices found and node has taint `nvidia.com/gpu=present:NoSchedule` applied by our init hook.

alex: do you have device-plugin logs? usually it's `nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset` on the node.

jamie: logs from the pod on that node:
```
I0825 07:42:11.123456   12345 device_plugin.go:210] Starting device plugin
E0825 07:42:12.123456   12345 plugin.go:87] failed to discover devices: failed to list devices: open /dev/nvidia0: no such file or directory
E0825 07:42:12.123456   12345 plugin.go:92] driver not ready
```
and `journalctl -u kubelet` shows repeated timeouts trying to probe devices. dmesg on node has repeated lines: "nvidia: init_module failed - Incorrect module version for kernel".

priya: that sounds like kernel/driver mismatch. Did the node image get a kernel upgrade recently? Preemptible nodes sometimes come from a different image when autoscaler creates them.

jamie: we patched the node-template image last week but we still see nodes created from the old template sometimes — suspected race between instance template rollout and the autoscaler. Also saw this in cloud-init when node boots: driver install script exits with code 1 because `/usr/src/linux-headers` doesn't match.

marco: CA behaviour: it sees NotReady and won't scale down healthy nodes, but also will not keep provisioning more because of perceived insufficient resources (it thinks pending pods fit on new machines but those nodes are unhealthy). Two problems: driver not installed before device plugin starts, and registration happens before modules available.

alex: quick mitigations:
- increase cluster-autoscaler `--max-node-provision-time` to 10m so nodes have time to run driver install scripts before being considered failed.
- add a readiness probe to device-plugin that reports NotReady until `/dev/nvidia0` exists (so node doesn't get tainted or scheduled prematurely).

priya: long term we should bake NVIDIA drivers into the node image or use a COS/AMI with driver pre-installed for GPU pools. Preemptible nodes are cheaper but riskier — maybe move critical production workloads to a dedicated non-preemptible pool.

jamie: tried `systemctl restart nvidia-dkms.service` as a manual fix on one node — it forced a reinstall of kernel module and node moved to Ready after ~2m. But that's not feasible at scale.

marco: also saw CA rapidly creating and deleting nodes because cloud provider returned heterogeneous images. We should gate autoscaler on a node-label (e.g., `image-ready=true`) until we confirm the instance-template rollout is complete.

alex: can we change our instance template to include a small init container that performs driver install and writes file `/var/lib/node-provision/driver-ready` before kubelet starts? Or set a systemd unit ordering so modules load prior to kubelet.

jamie: for an immediate workaround I disabled the `nvidia.com/gpu=present:NoSchedule` taint application by our init job (so the node won't be tainted until driver is present) — this prevents the weird scheduling semantics but we still need device plugin to succeed.

priya: another short-term idea: for preemptible pool set autoscaler `--scale-down-unneeded-time` higher and `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false`? hmm maybe not. More relevant is ensuring the provisioning time window is long enough and the startup script is robust to kernel header mismatches.

jamie: cost tradeoffs in the thread: preemptible saves ~60% but we pay in operational churn when drivers mismatch. For heavy steady workloads we should use reserved GPUs (Dedicated) — price vs reliability discussion to bring to product.

infra-bot: created issue INFRA-2238: "preemptible GPU nodes come up with driver/kernel mismatches causing NotReady; bake drivers into image + increase CA provision time" — link: https://redwood.internal/INFRA-2238

marco: action items we agreed on in call:
- bake tested NVIDIA driver into GPU node image and roll to preemptible pool (pri: high) — OWNER: eng-infra
- add device-plugin readiness gating and/or systemd ordering so kubelet starts after driver modules are loaded — OWNER: eng-runtime
- set CA `--max-node-provision-time=10m` for us-west clusters temporarily — OWNER: eng-platform
- evaluate moving critical workloads to Dedicated GPU pool and quantify monthly delta — OWNER: finance + product

jamie: tagging oncall to monitor next scale-up: @marco can you watch the autoscaler events for the next 2 hours? :eyes:

marco: on it. I'll post updates in this thread. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks — also adding a test in our CI that boots a node from the new instance-template and verifies `/dev/nvidia0` appears before kubelet registration.

jamie: great. will follow up in INFRA-2238 with logs and a list of nodes affected.
